Title: Billionaire investor Ray Dalio warns US debt nearing a breaking point

Summary: 
Billionaire investor Ray Dalio warned that the United States is approaching a "breaking point" in its debt trajectory, citing that the federal government will spend about $7 trillion this year while collecting only $5 trillion in revenue, a shortfall of roughly 40 %.

Dalio explained that the country’s debt now equals about six times its annual revenues. He projected that the Treasury will need to refinance or raise roughly $12 trillion in 2025 alone, including nearly $9 trillion in maturing debt and an additional $2 trillion to cover the deficit, with an extra $1 trillion consumed by interest payments—half the size of the current budget gap.

"Everyone I've spoken to agrees on the numbers and the mechanics," Dalio said, noting that the issue is widely acknowledged among policymakers and economists. He warned that the government has to move an enormous amount of debt and that "We're close to a breaking point."

Dalio proposed a "3 % solution" to reduce the deficit to roughly 3 % of GDP, down from its current 6‑7 %. This would require about 4 % more in taxes and 4 % less in spending. He cautioned that artificially forcing rates lower could scare off investors.

He also observed that tariffs are being used as a revenue tool and to protect domestic industries, but that they cannot solve the underlying imbalance. "As debt continues to grow, the supply‑demand dynamics will worsen to a point where they can't be corrected," he said.

Dalio concluded that unless leaders confront the hard choices of fiscal reform, the U.S. risks crossing a line where global confidence in America’s ability to manage its debt evaporates.
